compiled_state.title: Per-sub-branch reviewed batches for /debug-everything (sprint-parity ci-pr mode)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

The /debug-everything skill currently aggregates all fixes from a session (routinely 10-30 bug fixes) into a single undifferentiated PR. LLM reviewers cannot effectively review diffs of that size: reviewer fatigue degrades signal quality, token limits truncate context, and regressions slip past review. /sprint solved the analogous problem with per-story sub-PRs feeding a long-lived aggregate draft PR. Project maintainers and agents running /debug-everything sessions need the same architecture, with tier-class-appropriate batch sizing and parameterized reuse of sprint's shared machinery, so debug PRs ship with high-fidelity reviewed sub-components rather than one unreviewable monolith.

## Approach (Sprint-Parallel — Parameterize-then-Reuse)

Bundle rationale: parameterization is motivated solely by debug-everything reuse; regression-test discipline is identical for both halves; splitting would create implementation-time risk of the parameterization landing without a real second consumer exercising the new code paths.

1. /debug-everything reads the existing `merge.strategy` config key (values `direct` | `pr`). When `merge.strategy=pr`, /debug-everything activates ci-pr-mode sub-branch mechanics matching /sprint's pattern. When `merge.strategy=direct` (or absent), current single-session aggregated-commits behavior is preserved. Phase B Step 1 emits a one-line resolved-mode startup log. No new config key.
2. `.debug-active` marker created at Phase B Step 1 (when `merge.strategy=pr`), removed at Phase K. Phase A entry cleans stale markers (file present without matching live session-id pattern). Mid-session upgrade safety: if Phase A detects a marker pattern indicating a pre-upgrade in-flight session, refuse ci-pr operations until explicit restart.
3. `check-session-merge-only.sh` extended via additive OR guard for `.debug-active`; the existing `.sprint-active` evaluation is structurally unchanged. `DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0` escape hatch implemented as an independent conditional block (not OR-extended into `DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE`) with parallel audit-log file. The two escape hatches are independent.
4. Sub-branch machinery via parameterization, each with regression test verifying sprint defaults preserved end-to-end:
   - `create-story-branch.sh`: add `--prefix <name>` flag (default `story`); /debug-everything invokes `--prefix bug-batch`.
   - `detect-session-leakage.sh`: read `STORY_BRANCH_PREFIX` env var (default `story/`) for Case 1, Case 2, and Case 4 target/orphan branch construction (3 string-constructor lines).
   - `create-sprint-draft-pr.sh`: add `DRAFT_PR_TITLE_PREFIX` env var (default `Sprint:`) and `DRAFT_PR_BODY_TEMPLATE` env var (default to existing body); /debug-everything sets `Debug:` prefix.
   - `merge-story-branch.sh`: no parameterization required (audit confirms script writes `DSO-Story-Merge:` trailer, not `DSO-Story:` — no enforcement to parameterize).
   - Leak-detection cadence: `detect-session-leakage.sh` runs (a) after each fix-bug invocation in Bug-Fix Mode, (b) after each batch completion in Phase F/G, and (c) once at Phase K as a safety-net final sweep.
5. Sub-branch sizing by tier class:
   - Phase F (Tier 0-1 tool-atomic auto-fix): one sub-branch per tier (`bug-batch/<session-id>/tier-0`, `tier-1`), no count cap.
   - Phase G (Tier 2-7): ≤5 bugs per sub-branch, tier-first chunked (`bug-batch/<session-id>/tier-<N>-batch-<K>`), file-conflict splits.
   - Large-fix exception: single bug with estimated diff >500 lines gets its own `-large`-suffixed sub-branch.
   - Within a Phase G batch, sub-agent integration into the shared sub-branch ref is serialized at the orchestrator level.
6. `debug-session-id` format: `<UTC-timestamp>-<6-char-random>` (e.g., `20260512-141045-a3f9c2`) — prevents same-second collisions.
7. Durable state anchor: at each sub-branch creation, write `DEBUG_BRANCH_TRACKING: sub_branch=<name> tier=<N> batch=<K> timestamp=<UTC>` ticket comment on the debug session's epic. `COMPACTION_RESUME` fence reads most-recent comment to recover current sub-branch before any commit or fix-bug dispatch.
8. Discriminated sub-branch merge outcomes at Phase F/G loop level: `MERGED` (advance), `ESCALATED` (write `SUBBRANCH_ESCALATED:` ticket comment, continue to next sub-branch), `ERROR` (treat as ESCALATED). Per-mode instructions co-located in Bug-Fix Mode / Phase F / Phase G section headers; preamble drops cross-mode "uniformly" language.
9. Per-sub-branch scoped review invokes `validate-review-output.sh` JSON-schema validation before recording `REVIEW_RESULT`. Autonomous resolution loop honors `review.max_resolution_attempts` (default 5) with floor-guard: value 0 logs warning and uses minimum 1 attempt to prevent O(n) cascade-escalation on first finding.
10. Aggregate-PR coherence: when a sub-branch escalates, the aggregate draft PR description is annotated with `BLOCKED_SUBBRANCHES:` listing escalated sub-branches and reasons.

## Success Criteria

1. When /debug-everything runs with `merge.strategy=pr`, Phase B Step 1 (a) opens a long-lived aggregate draft PR via parameterized `create-sprint-draft-pr.sh` with `DRAFT_PR_TITLE_PREFIX=Debug:`, (b) creates a `.debug-active` marker containing the resolved `debug-session-id` (`<UTC-timestamp>-<6-char-random>`), (c) emits a one-line resolved-mode startup log. Marker removed at Phase K; Phase A removes stale markers whose embedded session-id has no matching live session.

2. Phase F (Tier 0-1 tool-atomic auto-fix) produces exactly one sub-branch per tier (`bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/tier-0` and `tier-1`) with no per-bug count chunking; entire tier's auto-fix output committed and reviewed as a single coherent change.

3. Phase G (Tier 2-7) chunks bugs into sub-branches named `bug-batch/<debug-session-id>/tier-<N>-batch-<K>` with at most 5 bugs per sub-branch, preserving tier ordering; file-conflict splits within a tier produce additional sub-branches without exceeding cap; any single bug whose estimated diff exceeds 500 lines is routed to its own `-large`-suffixed sub-branch. Within a Phase G batch, sub-agent integration into the shared sub-branch ref is serialized at the orchestrator level.

4. Each sub-branch passes its own scoped review before merging into session branch: (a) `validate-review-output.sh` JSON-schema validation against `reviewer-findings.json` before recording `REVIEW_RESULT`, (b) autonomous resolution loop with `review.max_resolution_attempts` (default 5; floor-guard 1 when configured 0), (c) discriminated `MERGED`/`ESCALATED`/`ERROR` outcome consumed at Phase F/G loop level. `ESCALATED` writes `SUBBRANCH_ESCALATED:` ticket comment, leaves sub-branch unmerged, continues to next sub-branch.

5. Direct non-merge commits to session worktree rejected by `check-session-merge-only.sh` when `.debug-active` is present; `DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0` escape hatch implemented as independent conditional block (mirroring `DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0`); existing `.sprint-active` code path structurally unchanged; concurrent sprint sessions unaffected. Tests added at `tests/hooks/test-check-session-merge-only.sh`: (a) `.debug-active` rejects non-merge commit, (b) both markers present rejects, (c) `DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0` permits, (d) existing sprint-active tests still pass. CLAUDE.md rule 24 updated to reflect `.debug-active` and `DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0` alongside sprint guidance.

6. After each fix-bug invocation (Bug-Fix Mode) and after each batch completion (Phase F single-tier batch, Phase G sub-branch batch), `detect-session-leakage.sh` runs against the current session-branch state and routes any leaked `DSO-Bug:`-trailed commits to matching `bug-batch/<...>` sub-branch via the 5-case matrix with `STORY_BRANCH_PREFIX=bug-batch/` env-var-parameterized target construction (Cases 1, 2, 4); trailerless or closed-bug-trailered commits surface manual attribution / `--force-route-to` resolution on stderr. Closed-bug-trailer race: when a sub-agent commit references a ticket closed during parallel batch execution, the script logs SHA + closed-ticket-id and routes to `--force-route-to`-pending rather than stalling. A final end-of-session sweep at Phase K runs as a safety net.

7. `merge.strategy=direct` (or absent) preserves current behavior end-to-end: no `.debug-active` marker, no hook rejection, no sub-branch creation, no aggregate draft PR. Resolved-mode startup log notes `"merge.strategy=direct — debug session running in local mode"` so an operator who intended PR mode but forgot to configure sees explicit evidence rather than silent fall-through.

8. Each sub-branch creation writes `DEBUG_BRANCH_TRACKING: sub_branch=<name> tier=<N> batch=<K> timestamp=<UTC>` ticket comment on the debug session's epic. `COMPACTION_RESUME` fence recovers current sub-branch from most-recent such comment before any commit or fix-bug dispatch.

9. Mechanism applies to Bug-Fix Mode, Phase F, Phase G — with instructions co-located in each mode's section header (not cross-mode preamble). Cap rule differs by mode per SC2/SC3.

10. Parameterization tasks land alongside this epic with regression tests verifying existing sprint defaults preserved end-to-end: `create-story-branch.sh --prefix <name>` (default `story`); `detect-session-leakage.sh STORY_BRANCH_PREFIX` env var (default `story/`); `create-sprint-draft-pr.sh DRAFT_PR_TITLE_PREFIX` (default `Sprint:`) and `DRAFT_PR_BODY_TEMPLATE` (default existing body). `merge-story-branch.sh` requires no parameterization (audit-confirmed no-op).

11. Hermetic-repro check (the pre-review test-isolation gate confirming a fix-bug RED test reproduces deterministically before commit, introduced by epic 99f1-153c at fix-bug Step 5) fires before per-sub-branch review dispatch; antipattern-scan output (99f1's static shell-pattern scanner at fix-bug Step 7.5 whose findings flag fragile constructs) captured as `Antipattern-Scan:` commit trailer on the sub-branch tip commit, visible in the per-sub-branch reviewer's diff context.

12. Debug-everything phases B, F, G, K enumerated in the forbidden-action registry (the config-driven list of git operations blocked by a PreToolUse hook inside active sprint/debug sessions, infrastructure introduced by epic af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81). PreToolUse hook reads both `.sprint-active` and `.debug-active` markers; `DSO_DEBUG_ACTIVE=0` escape hatch honored alongside `DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0`.

13. Per-sub-branch review invokes `validate-review-output.sh` JSON-schema validation (validates `reviewer-findings.json` conforms to published schema, infrastructure shipped by epic 677d-a6a0) before recording `REVIEW_RESULT`. Schema-correction re-dispatch (677d's existing re-dispatch loop on schema failure) handled mid-resolution-loop with re-validation before merge. SC13 depends on 677d being closed before this epic enters Phase F sprint execution; if 677d not closed at sprint time, SC13 descopes to a follow-on story re-parented under this epic.

14. Before closing the epic, run a reference /debug-everything session in PR mode against a branch with ≥8 staged bug fixes; record sub-branch count (target ≥3), per-sub-branch review verdicts (target ≥95% pass without escalation), and total token spend. Baseline protocol: re-run the identical bug-ID list through /debug-everything with `merge.strategy=direct` on a clean branch immediately before or after the PR-mode run; token spend recorded from session log in both cases. Acceptance: PR-mode sub-branch count ≥3; sub-branch pass-rate ≥95%; PR-mode token spend no more than local-mode token spend within 5% measurement variance.

## Scenario Analysis (surviving)

- **Parallel commit race in Phase G** (high, runtime) — addressed by SC3 serialization clause.
- **Aggregate PR diverges on partial-tier escalation** (medium, runtime) — addressed by Approach item 10 BLOCKED_SUBBRANCHES annotation.
- **Closed-bug-trailer parallel-load misroute** (high, runtime) — addressed by SC6 force-route-to-pending clause + earlier leak-detection cadence.
- **Pre-upgrade in-flight sessions** (medium, deployment) — addressed by Approach item 2 refusal protocol.
- **merge.strategy unset → local silent fall-through** (medium, configuration) — addressed by SC7 explicit-log clause.
- **review.max_resolution_attempts=0 cascade** (medium, configuration) — addressed by SC4 floor-guard.

## Dependencies

- Epic 677d-a6a0-0c2e-4b9e (CI llm-review schema validation): SC13 prerequisite; descopes if not closed at sprint time.
- No other blocking dependencies.

## Follow-on (separate tickets, not blockers)

- `check-session-branch-invariant.sh` (hardcoded `story/` grep pattern) and `worktree-cleanup.sh` (hardcoded `story/*` in CONFIG_ORPHAN_PATTERNS) do not currently cover `bug-batch/` branches. File as follow-on bug tickets for eventual parity. Out of scope for this epic.
